title: מר עוקבא

paragraphs:
Mar Ukva, court head in Shemuel's days, Rashi Kiddushin 44b and Shabbat 108b: he and his court at Kafri. Rashi, Mo'ed Katan 16b, calls him nasi; Tosafot Sanhedrin 31b, exilarch. In judgment Ukva sat above Shemuel, while in study he sat before Shemuel at a distance of four cubits—Rashi: Shemuel was his Torah teacher. He escorted Mar Shemuel to his lodging, Mo'ed Katan 16b. Shemuel told Rav Yehudah: 'Sharp one, your head in cold, your head's head in hot; Mar Ukva and his court are still present,' Shabbat 55a. Ketubbot 67b: accustomed to miracles; at his death they found (seven) thousand gold dinars given in charity. Saying the road was long and provisions light, he gave away a third—should read half—of his property. Although one should not give more than a fifth, at death one may.

They wrote, 'To him whose radiance resembles Batyah's son, peace: Ukvan the Babylonian complained of his brother Yirmeyah obstructing his way'—meaning castrating him—and told the court to compel him to appear in Tiberias [השיאוהו, as Rashi explains], Sanhedrin 31b. They say he was the penitent Natan deTzutzita; see there, for this is not so. See part 1, 4757, for the notice on Ukvan deTzutzita [י״ע, apparently Yesod Olam, named in the preceding line]. Geniva distressed him; he wrote R. Elazar [source spelling אלעור] about his adversaries, whom he could hand to the government. R. Elazar answered to wait silently for God and attend the study house morning and evening against them. Geniva was immediately put in a neck-chain, Gittin 7a; see there. He called himself vinegar son of wine: his father waited a full day after meat before cheese, while he ate it at another meal, Ḥullin 105a. His brother-in-law died; he planned seven- and thirty-day mourning. Rav Huna asked whether he wanted mourning food: mourning in his wife's honor applied only to father- and mother-in-law, Mo'ed Katan 20b. He gave a poor neighbor four zuz daily through the door-hole. The man wished to identify him; Ukva fled into a fiery oven rather than shame him, Ketubbot 67b. Gilgulei Neshamot, Mem §13 [source ג״נ], calls Ukva a spark of Yehudah and his wife of Tamar. Tamar, 'she was being brought out,' refused to shame Yehudah. Hence the saying: better to cast oneself into a fiery furnace, etc.

In Abba, Shemuel's father's name. R. Oshaya in his name. Rav Aḥa bar Yosef came before him. Rav Huna spoke to him (see above), and in his name, Jerusalem Talmud, Shevi'it 7. R. Zeira in his name, Shabbat 108b. R. Zakkai said. Rav Ḥanina permitted him, Ketubbot 60b. Rav Ḥisda in his name, Berakhot 29b; Shabbat 116b, 119b; Eruvin 21b; Gittin 88a; Avodah Zarah 17a; Pesaḥim 40a; Arakhin 15b. Tavi in his time. R. Tavi bar Meri; Tava in his name. Before R. Yehoshua ben Levi, arranging aggadah, Berakhot 10a. R. Ukva בשריב״ל [relationship/abbreviation unresolved], Jerusalem Talmud פ״ר [locator unresolved]. Rav Yosef (see his entry); R. Yosef bar Abba in his name. R. Yannai the elder sent to him, Shabbat 108b. R. Yirmeyah in his name. Bar Levai before him. In R. Levi's name, Shabbat there. Lili bar Mani in his name; Mari bar Mar in his name. Rav Anan addressed him as Mar. Rava spoke and objected; the answer is after he heard from R. Akiva. Tosafot corrects this to Mar Ukva and says elsewhere too Rava lived in Ukva's time, Nazir 53a. This is very puzzling: Ukva was Shemuel's colleague, and Rava was born when Shemuel's student Rav Yehudah died. How could Ukva live until Rava heard him? I would correct it to Rav Akavya, of whom Rava says, ‘Who is wise like Rav Akavya?’ (see his entry), rather than Mar Ukva. Better still, Tosafot's 'in Mar Ukva's time' should read 'bar Ukva's time,' since Rava declared bar Ukva's sons' ox a terefah, Ḥullin 43b; see there. Shemuel said, Shabbat 109a; in Shemuel's name, Eruvin 81a; Rosh HaShanah 22a; Yevamot 12a, 76a. He frequented R. Shimon ben Pazi.
